response_text:
Short version first:
- Azure error: you used Azure model strings like "azure/gpt-4". Azure OpenAI wants the *deployment name* (the deployment you created on your resource), not the provider-prefixed model name. Azure returned DeploymentNotFound (404).
- Anthropic error: the Anthropic request ended up missing/invalid model id. Use Anthropic's raw model ID (no provider prefix), e.g. "claude-..." (or your exact Anthropic model id).
- Groq error: max_tokens (32768) exceeds that model's context window (8192). Lower max_tokens to ≤ context window (or use a model that supports 32k).

1) Diagnose each error

Error Type 1 — Azure OpenAI (azure-gpt4, azure-gpt4-mini)
- Root cause
  - litellm_params.model is set to "azure/..." (provider-prefixed) instead of the Azure deployment name you created in the Azure OpenAI resource.
- Why this error
  - Azure OpenAI API calls are routed to a deployment (URL: /openai/deployments/{deployment}/...). If the deployment name in the request doesn't match any deployment on that resource, Azure returns DeploymentNotFound (404). Using "azure/gpt-4" produced a deployment id that doesn't exist on the contoso resource.

Error Type 2 — Anthropic (claude-opus, claude-sonnet)
- Root cause
  - litellm_params.model is given as "anthropic/..." rather than the Anthropic model id expected by Anthropic's API.
- Why this error
  - The Anthropic API requires the JSON body to include a valid "model" value (its model id). The provider-prefixed value or wrong formatting resulted in a request that did not include a valid model id (Anthropic responded "model: field required" 400).

Error Type 3 — Groq (llama-fast, llama-mini)
- Root cause
  - max_tokens was set to 32768 while the selected Groq models have an 8192 token context window.
- Why this error
  - Providers reject requests where requested max_tokens > model context window. Groq returned an invalid_request_error pointing out the mismatch.

2) Fixed config (changed lines only)

Group B — Azure OpenAI (change model to your actual deployment name; replace placeholders with the exact deployment names you created in Azure)
```yaml
# for model_name: azure-gpt4
litellm_params:
  model: "<AZURE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_FOR_GPT4>"      # was: azure/gpt-4

# for model_name: azure-gpt4-mini
litellm_params:
  model: "<AZURE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_FOR_GPT4O_MINI>" # was: azure/gpt-4o-mini
```

Group C — Anthropic (use Anthropic model ids, no provider prefix; replace placeholders if needed)
```yaml
# for model_name: claude-opus
litellm_params:
  model: "claude-opus-4"   # was: anthropic/claude-opus-4-20250514

# for model_name: claude-sonnet
litellm_params:
  model: "claude-sonnet-4" # was: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514
```
(If your account uses different Anthropic model IDs, use those exact IDs.)

Group E — Groq (reduce max_tokens to the model's context window or lower)
```yaml
# for model_name: llama-fast
litellm_params:
  max_tokens: 8192   # was: 32768

# for model_name: llama-mini
litellm_params:
  max_tokens: 8192   # was: 32768
```

3) Validation checklist — commands / checks to verify fixes

General first steps after editing config:
- Restart LiteLLM (or reload config) and watch logs for errors:
  - docker restart <litellm_container> OR systemctl restart litellm OR however you run it
  - tail -f <litellm logs> and confirm the previous 400/404 errors disappear.

Azure-specific checks:
- Confirm the deployment names in Azure Portal: Open your OpenAI resource → Deployments and note exact names (case-sensitive).
- Quick API smoke test (replace placeholders):
  curl -s -X POST "https://contoso.openai.azure.com/openai/deployments/<DEPLOYMENT_NAME>/chat/completions?api-version=2024-02-15-preview" \
    -H "api-key: $AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}],"max_tokens":1}'
  - Expect HTTP 200 and a short completion.
- Send a test request through LiteLLM to the azure-gpt4 model (use your proxy/test client) and verify a successful reply and no DeploymentNotFound errors in logs.

Anthropic-specific checks:
- Direct API smoke test (replace model id and API key):
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.anthropic.com/v1/complete" \
    -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"claude-opus-4","prompt":"Human: Hello\n\nAssistant:","max_tokens_to_sample":1}'
  - Expect HTTP 200 and a small completion (or use Anthropic's current endpoint/fields per their docs).
- Run the same minimal request via LiteLLM against model_name "claude-opus" and confirm success and no “model: field required” errors.

Groq-specific checks:
- Confirm the model's context window from Groq docs or console (you saw 8192 in the error).
- Directly test the model with a small request:
  curl -s -X POST "https://api.groq.com/v1/models/<model-id>/outputs" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $GROQ_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"input":"Hello","max_output_tokens":8}'
  - Expect HTTP 200.
- Send a test through LiteLLM to the relevant model_name (llama-fast / llama-mini) with max_tokens small or up to 8192, confirm success.

Other useful checks:
- Validate env vars used in config exist (quick shell check):
  echo $AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY && echo $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY && echo $GROQ_API_KEY
- Confirm LiteLLM startup logs show successful client initializations for each provider (no auth/setup errors).

4) Prevention — CI/config validation to catch these before deployment

Add these automated checks to your CI or pre-deploy pipeline:

Azure
- Deployment-existence check: for each config entry pointing at an Azure api_base, call the resource's deployments endpoint or attempt a minimal /openai/deployments/{name}/chat/completions request using the provided api_key and api_version. Fail if 404.
- Enforce config pattern: require that Azure model strings do not include a provider prefix (reject "azure/...") or validate and map them explicitly.

Anthropic
- Per-provider schema validation: ensure Anthropic entries set model to a non-empty string matching expected Anthropic ID patterns (no provider prefix). Optionally run a tiny validation request to Anthropic to confirm the model resolves.
- Fail the pipeline if Anthropic responds with model-related errors to the validation call.

Groq (and other providers)
- Constrain numeric fields: validate max_tokens ≤ known model context window. Either:
  - Query provider model metadata in CI to get exact context size, or
  - Maintain a trusted mapping (model -> max_context) in CI and validate config values.
- Reject obviously too-large values (e.g., > 65536) as a guardrail.

General
- Add a "litellm config lint/validate" CI step that:
  - Validates YAML schema (required keys present, correct types).
  - Verifies required env vars are set (fail fast).
  - Does provider-specific light probes (minimal request with max_tokens=1) to verify credentials and model/deployment exist.
- Keep config values explicit and use placeholders in repo (do not commit secrets). Use a separate secrets store for actual keys.
- Add unit/integration tests that spin a temporary LiteLLM instance with the config and run one small request per model (fast, low-cost) to catch API-level errors.

If you want, I can:
- Produce a small validation script (bash/python) that reads your litellm_config.yaml and performs the pre-deploy checks above (Azure deployment existence, Anthropic model validation, Groq max_tokens check).
